caveat: Measured from CARR's own annotations (CC BY 4.0, doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.29470079.v3) -- no model inference. Frames are independent samples from a single tilted camera per store, so this is an engagement MIX, not a conversion funnel, and positions are normalised camera-frame coordinates, not floor metres. Class volumes reflect how the dataset was collected, not how often each behaviour happens in a real shop.
insight: 'Picking And Returning' is the most common single behaviour observed. The gap between looking and handling is the clearest early signal of what is actually wanted, well before anything reaches the counter.

actions.observed: In 51% (about 5 in every 10) of the moments we watched, somebody had their hands on the stock. The rest were looking or moving on.
actions.todo: Track this number week to week. If it falls, the stock stopped appealing before anyone reached the counter -- and the till will not tell you that for another month.
